subject: Linguistics
title: Political Language
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Political Language.

hook.text: 'Collateral damage' means civilians were killed. Political language hides harsh realities behind soft words.

buildup.text: Politicians use euphemisms, framing, and loaded language to shape public perception.

discovery.text: George Lakoff showed that 'tax relief' frames taxes as an affliction—the framing wins the debate.

twist.text: Orwell warned that political language 'is designed to make lies sound truthful and murder respectable.'

climax.text: Critical discourse analysis reveals how language constructs power relations, not just reflects them.

punchline.text: The words chosen shape the reality perceived.

quiz.question: What is framing in political language?
options: Choosing words that shape perception of an issue
